notes:
**The AI was told on every single compile that you had never run the data check** - including a minute after you ran it. The check asks your own broker what history it will actually serve, and the whole point is to stop the model writing rules against data you do not have. The answer was measured, shown to you, and thrown away before the one thing that could use it. It is saved now, and it is the exact sentences you were shown, so the model cannot be told something different from the screen.

**The recorder's candles were a pool the backtest never read.** The recorder starts with the app and writes every candle it sees, because a session it misses is history no broker will serve again. The archive backtests read is a different file, and the function that folds one into the other was written, tested, and called by nothing. It now runs once a day at startup - so the sessions built from live ticks finally count toward your backtests.
